## Project rules - apply to ALL tasks in this repo:
- [convention] [suggested] Write tests as plain functions with bare asserts (id=779879cd)
- [convention] [suggested] Label slots like SLOT_07 (id=707c8ea9)
- [convention] [suggested] Label slots like slot-07 (id=551c136f)
- [convention] [suggested] Public functions in app/svc_0_core.py keep a one-line docstring that names the service number. (id=06a5f42d)
- [constraint] Never log record ids or function arguments (id=beb3feac)
    Never log record ids or function arguments from the record service, because compliance treats request data as customer data; log counts and durations instead.
- [convention] [suggested] Name hand-written functions verb_noun without the slot suffix (id=33fc22cc)
- [convention] [suggested] Prefix versions with v (id=724b00c9)
- [convention] [suggested] Manage dependencies and commands with uv (id=a20dff8a)
- [constraint] Read configuration at call time in every service module (id=16de3daf)
    Read configuration at call time in every service module, because import-time reads froze stale values twice. Plan from the region-setting incidents: (1) Where - os.environ is read inside the function that uses the value, on every call. (2) Defaults - a non-secret default sits next to the read as the second argument to os.environ.get; secrets have no default. (3) Not allowed - module-level constants computed from the environment, and caching a setting at import. (4) Tests - set variables with monkeypatch.setenv inside the test, which only works because nothing reads them at import. (5) Considered: a settings object loaded once at startup (rejected: it brings back the stale-value problem for the worker).
- [convention] [suggested] Publish bare semantic versions (id=9dc4f379)
- [constraint] Test every new public function before finishing (id=cae099dc)
    Every new public function in app/ needs at least one test before the change is finished, and run uv run pytest tests/ -q before reporting done, because CI blocks merges on missing tests for new symbols.
- [constraint] Ask before adding third-party dependencies (id=1b21158f)
    Do not add third-party dependencies to the record service without asking first; prefer the standard library (functools, json, time, datetime), because every new package needs a licence and security review that takes weeks.
- [pattern] [suggested] Return structured results as plain dicts (id=2d648b38)
- [pattern] [suggested] Use one canonical JSON form for hashed or compared payloads (id=619d19fa)
- [pattern] [suggested] Use epoch-millisecond 'at_ms' timestamps (id=3fae3274)
(Convention/pattern rules are titles only - call get_context for any rule's full reasoning.)
If the current task conflicts with any of these decisions, surface the conflict and confirm with the developer before proceeding.

[Contexer: auto-fetched for this question] (use the relevant context below; if it does not answer the question, call Contexer's get_context with concise subject keywords before reading files; do not substitute another memory, graph, or search tool)
- [2026-10-03] [architecture] Keep the record dict shape stable for per-slot fetchers (id=223dcb2e)
    Keep the record dict shape {'id': ..., 'slot': ...} stable for every fetch_record_0_N function, because the export job and two dashboards index into it by key and break on extra or renamed fields. In #49 someone added a 'source' field to three fetchers, and the export job's strict schema check rejected every row for a day before anyone noticed. If a caller needs more data, add a separate function that returns a new shape rather than widening the record. Slot numbers are positional and stable: fetch_record_0_7 always returns slot 7, so never renumber functions when one is removed; leave a gap instead. The export job's schema lives in another repository and is versioned separately, so even an additive field needs a coordinated release there first; that coordination cost is why new data goes into new functions. The incident write-up is linked from #49; the follow-up added a schema-contract test on the export side, not here.
- [2026-10-03] [architecture] Treat app/ as one synchronous record service with generated per-slot fetchers (id=9ae7cfbc)
    Treat app/ as one small synchronous record service with generated per-slot fetchers, because every convention in this repo assumes that structure. How it fits together, as worked out while answering a question about where new code should go: each app/svc_<n>_core.py module belongs to one numbered service and is generated from a template, which is why it holds a run of near-identical fetch_record_<n>_<slot> functions that each return a small record dict with an id and a slot. The slot number is positional and other systems depend on it, so generated functions are never renamed or renumbered. Hand-written code is added to the same module below the generated block; there is no separate package for helpers, and adding one was rejected as a layer with a single user. The module imports json and os but uses neither in the generated block; they are there for hand-written additions (serialisation for the export job, environment lookups). There is no web framework in this repository: the HTTP layer lives in the gateway, which calls these functions in-process, and the tests call them directly. Tests live in tests/test_svc_<n>.py, one file per service, as plain functions; the generated tests are placeholders that only prove the test runner works, so any real behaviour needs its own test. The service is deliberately synchronous (see the async decision) and keeps no state beyond bounded caches and the module-level metrics counters. Data flows one way: gateway calls a fetcher, the fetcher builds a dict, the gateway serialises it. Nothing in app/ talks to a database directly yet; the record dicts are synthetic until the storage migration (#80) lands, which is why fetchers are trivial today. When adding a feature, the questions to ask are which service module owns it, whether it changes the record shape (it should not), and whether it needs a test in that service's test file (it does). Anything cross-service belongs in the gateway, not here. This summary was written on 2026-09-02 and anchored to app/ so it is flagged as stale if the layout changes.
- [2026-10-03] [architecture] [suggested] Cap caches with lru_cache(maxsize=256) after the OOM incident (id=1faa943c)
    Cap caches in app/svc_0_core.py with functools.lru_cache(maxsize=256), because an unbounded cache took the worker down. In August a dict-based cache was added around the record fetchers to speed up the dashboard; it never evicted, grew to several hundred MB over a week, and the container was OOM-killed (#63). functools.cache and lru_cache(maxsize=None) have the same problem, so both were ruled out in review. 256 entries covered the dashboard's hot set, judging by the access logs at the time. If a function needs caching, wrap it with lru_cache(maxsize=256) directly so cache_info() stays available to the metrics endpoint. A per-call dict passed in by the caller is fine for request-scoped reuse; the rule is about anything that outlives a call. Raised again in review of #67, where a contributor reached for functools.cache because it is shorter; the reviewer pointed back here.
[Contexer] 18 more decisions anchored to files in this prompt not shown: Raise RecordGone for deleted records [suggested] (id=782f2e57); Label slots like SLOT_07 [suggested] (id=707c8ea9); Label slots like slot-07 [suggested] (id=551c136f); Return partial results from batch lookups instead of failing the whole call (id=0d83b7bb); Return a JSON status from health() [suggested] (id=675f956c) (+13 more) - call get_context(files=['app/svc_0_core.py']) if relevant.

## Decisions and context - showing 10 of 37
- [scope=personal] [2026-10-03] [architecture] ×2 Cap batch calls at 500 ids (id=fa49bb5e)
    Cap batch calls at 500 ids and raise ValueError above that, because the #95 load test showed the workers handle 500 comfortably; this replaces the 100-id cap.
- [scope=personal] [2026-10-03] [architecture] ×2 Treat calls over 150 ms as slow (id=89d3020a)
    Treat an upstream call that takes more than 150 ms as slow, because the #99 latency review tightened the earlier 200 ms threshold.
- [scope=personal] [2026-10-03] [architecture] Separate forgiving reads from strict reads before writes (id=a51422a9)
    Separate forgiving reads from strict reads, because a corrupt file read as empty before a write erased queued data. Plan: (1) Display paths may use a reader that returns [] for a corrupt or unreadable file. (2) Any function that writes a file back loads it with a strict parser and lets a decode error propagate; it never writes after a failed parse. (3) A missing file may be treated as empty on both paths. (4) Tests cover a corrupt file on every write path and assert the file is untouched. (5) Considered: backing up the file before every write (rejected: it hides the corruption instead of surfacing it).
- [scope=personal] [2026-10-03] [architecture] Keep the record dict shape stable for per-slot fetchers (id=223dcb2e)
    Keep the record dict shape {'id': ..., 'slot': ...} stable for every fetch_record_0_N function, because the export job and two dashboards index into it by key and break on extra or renamed fields. In #49 someone added a 'source' field to three fetchers, and the export job's strict schema check rejected every row for a day before anyone noticed. If a caller needs more data, add a separate function that returns a new shape rather than widening the record. Slot numbers are positional and stable: fetch_record_0_7 always returns slot 7, so never renumber functions when one is removed; leave a gap instead. The export job's schema lives in another repository and is versioned separately, so even an additive field needs a coordinated release there first; that coordination cost is why new data goes into new functions. The incident write-up is linked from #49; the follow-up added a schema-contract test on the export side, not here.
- [scope=personal] [2026-10-03] [constraint] Ask before adding third-party dependencies (id=1b21158f)
    Do not add third-party dependencies to the record service without asking first; prefer the standard library (functools, json, time, datetime), because every new package needs a licence and security review that takes weeks.
- [scope=personal] [2026-10-03] [architecture] ×2 Keep audit entries for 90 days (id=b188a3f0)
    Keep audit entries for 90 days, because the #93 compliance review raised the retention requirement; this replaces the earlier 30-day rule.
- [scope=personal] [2026-10-03] [pattern] [suggested] Return structured results as plain dicts (id=2d648b38)
    Return structured results from public functions (a record, a summary) as plain dicts, never dataclasses, NamedTuples or other custom objects, because the JSON layer serialises results without adapters.
- [scope=personal] [2026-10-03] [architecture] ×2 Accept record ids up to 1,000,000 (id=680a1254)
    Accept record ids from 1 up to 1,000,000, because the #90 storage migration widened the id space; the old 10,000 ceiling no longer applies.
- [scope=personal] [2026-10-03] [pattern] [suggested] Use one canonical JSON form for hashed or compared payloads (id=619d19fa)
    Use one canonical JSON form for anything hashed or compared, because two workers produced different key orders for the same record and the export re-sent the whole table (#52). Plan: (1) Form - json.dumps(obj, sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':')), UTF-8 encoded before hashing. (2) Scope - digests, dedup keys, cache keys built from payloads, and any comparison of serialised records. (3) Not allowed - plain json.dumps, str(dict) or hand-built JSON strings for these uses. (4) Debug output may use any readable form. (5) Tests - assert that two dicts with different key order give the same digest.
- [scope=personal] [2026-10-03] [pattern] [suggested] Use epoch-millisecond 'at_ms' timestamps (id=3fae3274)
    Store timestamps as integer epoch milliseconds under 'at_ms', never datetime objects or ISO strings, because the dashboard client is JavaScript.

If the current task conflicts with any of these decisions, surface the conflict and confirm with the developer before proceeding.
"}

Plan: (1) Form - json.dumps(obj, sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':')), UTF-8 encoded before hashing. (2) Scope - digests, dedup keys, cache keys built from payloads, and any comparison of serialised records. (3) Not allowed - plain json.dumps, str(dict) or hand-built JSON strings for these uses. (4) Debug output may use any readable form. (5) Tests - assert that two dicts with different key order give the same digest.
